title: MOVE: Or When the Philly Police Dropped a Bomb on a Residential Neighborhood
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the MOVE bombing in Philadelphia. They trace the origins of MOVE, the group led by John Africa, with its back-to-nature, anti-technology and animal-rights philosophy and its confrontational presence in a West Philadelphia neighborhood. They describe the 1978 standoff and police shooting, the bitter feud with the police, the 1985 siege on Osage Avenue in which police used water cannons, tear gas and about ten thousand rounds of gunfire, and the decision to drop a bomb from a helicopter that started a fire that destroyed the block. They discuss the deaths of eleven people including six children, the survivors Ramona and Michael Ward (Birdie Africa), the officer James Burghardt who tried to rescue Birdie, the commission and lack of criminal punishment, the civil settlements, and what happened to the MOVE members afterward. The episode ends with a listener email and a sign-off.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Ticket plug and opening
segments.summary: Josh plugs upcoming tour dates in Chicago and Toronto, then introduces the episode as the first of an 'I can't believe this happened' series and previews the Philadelphia police bombing of MOVE.

segments.title: MOVE origins and philosophy
segments.summary: The hosts describe MOVE, its leader John Africa, the adoption of the Africa surname, its animal-rights and anti-system philosophy, its raw-food and anti-technology rules, and its presence in a West Philadelphia row house neighborhood.

segments.title: Neighborhood conflict and loudspeakers
segments.summary: The hosts discuss MOVE's loudspeakers, neighbors' complaints and alleged threats, the Black Power connection, and the debate over whether MOVE was a cult.

segments.title: Background: Rizzo era and 1978 standoff
segments.summary: The hosts cover Mayor Frank Rizzo's tough approach, the 1978 standoff in which a police officer was killed, the baby's death during an earlier confrontation, and the police raid that led to the MOVE nine's imprisonment and the beating of Delbert Africa.

segments.title: Children and conditions inside MOVE house
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the treatment of children in MOVE, including raw food rules and hidden toys, and testimony from Michael Ward (Birdie Africa) about his experience.

segments.title: Mayor Goode and the 1985 siege begins
segments.summary: The hosts describe Mayor Wilson Goode's reform background and his response to the MOVE nine raid, then the plan to remove MOVE from the Osage Avenue house, neighbors being evacuated, and the water cannon and tear gas attempts that failed.

segments.title: Gunfire, the bomb and the fire
segments.summary: Police fire thousands of rounds at the house, the bomb squad proposes dropping a bomb, C4 supplied by the FBI is mentioned, a helicopter drops a satchel charge, and the fire spreads with a delayed order to put it out and Sambor's testimony.

segments.title: Escape attempt, aftermath and settlements
segments.summary: The hosts describe the escape attempt and gunfire in the alley, officer James Burghardt's rescue of Birdie, the death toll of eleven including six children, civil settlements, the criminal punishments, and later fates of the survivors and MOVE members.

segments.title: Listener email: perfect pitch
segments.summary: A listener named Kenny shares a story about a band recording a song with a pitch mismatch, and the hosts respond.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners, give contact information, and close the episode.
